title: Why Did France Want Vietnam So Badly?
fullText: if you look at a map of Asia in 1887 you'll notice something odd sitting on China's southern border this all of it French which is strange because the regional superpower was Britain sitting right next door in India and Burma and France's previous attempts  at empire building in Asia amounted to roughly nothing which raises the obvious question why did France want Vietnam so badly why did a country still digging itself out from under a German invasion spend 30 years and a small fortune conquering an empire on the other side of the planet so France's involvement in Vietnam started earlier than you'd think 1787 when a French missionary calling himself Pinio de Bayen walked into Versailles with a seven year old Vietnamese prince and talked Louis the 16th into backing the boy's fugitive father in a civil war France signed promised ships and troops and then delivered none of them because it was two years away from having a revolution of its own the bishop rounded up volunteers and mercenaries anyway the prince's father won and he crowned himself Emperor Zia Long founder of the Nowin dynasty so France helped install the exact dynasty it would later spend three decades dismantling efficient by the 1850s that dynasty had turned hard against the Catholics France had shipped over and in 1857 Emperor to duck had a bishop beheaded  a Spanish one Jose Maria Diaz which is why the eventual French invasion also included Spanish troops from Manila Catholic sources claim tens of thousands of Christians died in the purges a figure other historians dispute either way Paris was outraged and a lobbying bishop named Pellarin personally pitched Napoleon the third on intervention conveniently France already had a fleet in the neighborhood fighting the Second Opium War alongside Britain so in September 1858 14 warships showed up at Danang to deliver some civilization the plan was simple  take the port march on the capital  and make two duck sign things the Vietnamese instead surrounded the port and kept the French bottled up there for a year and a half  until they evacuated about 1,000 Frenchmen died mostly of disease which the brochures had failed to mention unable to go home empty handed the French sailed south and took Saigon instead and by 1862 two duc handed over three southern provinces just to make them stop and there France sat until the freelancers arrived in 1873 an officer named Francis Garnier captured Hanoi with 180 men  and zero authorization then got himself killed by the black flags Chinese irregulars working for the Vietnamese a month later Paris apologized and handed everything back nine years later another officer Henri Riviere did the exact same thing  and died the exact same way at this point Paris decided that repeatedly conquering and unconquering Hanoi was bad optics  and went all in so why did France actually want Vietnam well the first reason was prestige after Prussia flattened France in 1871 its leaders concluded the fastest way to look like a great power again was to own large amounts of the map and Prime Minister Jules Ferry who told Parliament that superior races had a duty to civilise inferior ones made Vietnam the flagship project also there was China The Red River ran from Hanoi straight into southern China and French merchants were convinced it was a back door to 400 million customers and on top of that Catholicism gave the whole enterprise a Halo France wasn't conquering anyone you understand it was protecting missionaries Protection that happened to come with tax collection attached the problem was that Vietnam was on paper a tributary of China and China objected with soldiers the result was an undeclared war in 1884 which the French navy mostly won and the French public entirely hated and in March 1885 a panicky telegram about a retreat from one border town a retreat that was militarily speaking barely a setback but the telegram made it sound like a catastrophe reached Paris Parliament erupted and crowds outside chanted death to the Tonkinese by which they meant ferry and his allies since Tonkinese had become Parisian shorthand for anyone wasting French lives overseas his government collapsed the same afternoon he never held power again nine months later the chamber of deputies voted on whether to abandon Vietnam altogether keeping it won 274 to 270 if four deputies had changed their minds there'd be no French Indochina no colony  no "Điện Biên Phủ" of what followed one French historian later summed it up France acquired Indochina very much against its own wishes the empire nobody voted for except for the four guys who did so that patch of French territory on China's doorstep it existed because of a bishop who wouldn't take no for an answer two officers who couldn't follow instructions and the narrowest parliamentary vote in colonial history France would keep all of it until 1954 when a valley called "Điện Biên Phủ" ended the arrangement  rather abruptly but that's a whole other episode
